What are FIS and FLM?
The teacher behind this path

This course is built on Dr. Bardia Khosravani’s FIS method (Rose educational collection): fundamental investing with Codal, focused on dividend-focused stocks, for passive income and financial freedom.

Boxes that start with “In Dr. Khosravani’s words” are his own sentences from his blog, videos and public channel, with their sources (translated from Persian in this English edition). The rest of the text is this app’s explanation of his teachings.
He did not make or endorse this app. His full courses are at the Rose educational collection (roseoj.com).
Two Wings of One Bird

FIS: Dr. Bardia Khosravani’s Fundamental Investing System; fundamental analysis to find real, profitable businesses on the Tehran Stock Exchange and Farabourse by reading official Codal disclosures, with a focus on dividend-focused stocks.
FLM: the other side of the coin; managing fear and greed, biases, position size, and fitting investing to your financial life.
FIS is not technical analysis or short-term trading.
Know Before You Start
This app is educational and is not investment advice.
No method, FIS included, guarantees a profit. The goal: fewer big mistakes and better odds of a positive real return over the long run.
Company names in the examples are made up. Where details of a rule or of Codal’s menus are uncertain, they are marked “(please check)”.
The 6-Stage Roadmap
0. Personal readiness (1 week) → personal investment statement
1. Foundations (2 weeks) → understanding real return and market structure
2. Codal (3 to 4 weeks) → a complete file on 3 companies
3. FIS skills (6 to 8 weeks) → a sustainable-earnings model and valuation for 5 companies
4. Full FLM (alongside stage 3) → written rules
5. Integrated practice (6 to 8 weeks) → a 3-month paper portfolio
6. Advanced (4 weeks) → analysis of one holding company and one currency-earning company
What exactly does FIS do?
It reads official disclosures to find and value real, profitable businesses
It uses chart patterns and trading volume to predict the price direction in coming days
It follows retail money inflows and buy queues to spot hot stocks early
FIS is fundamental analysis: real profit, value and business risk. Charts and signals are not part of it.
Which one is part of FLM?
Managing fear in a market drop, and position size
Calculating gross margin
Reading the cost-of-sales note and calculating each quarter’s margin
FLM means psychology and financial life: emotions, biases, position size, long-term holding and fitting your personal needs.
If applied correctly, the FIS method guarantees a profit.
No method guarantees a profit. FIS lowers the chance of a big mistake; it does not make risk zero.

Practising with Live Codal
Practice List and Folder
8 to 10 companies from 4 different industries (for example cement, petrochemicals, pharma, banking, steel, food). Each industry has a different report format and risk.

For each company, one spreadsheet with 4 sheets: “Monthly” (volume, rate, amount), “Quarterly” (profit and loss for each 3 months), “Events” (capital increases, general meetings, material announcements) and “Decision journal”.
Routine and Habits
30 minutes every week: open the new announcements on Codal, enter the numbers, and only then look at the price on tsetmc. Numbers first, price second.
Before a report comes out, forecast your own number and write it down. Forecast error is the best teacher.
At least 3 months of paper portfolio with written reasons, compared with the overall index and a fixed-income fund.

Saving the FIS Way
Set savings aside at the start of the month, not from whatever is left at the end.

In Dr. Khosravani’s view, traditional saving (a deposit or a fixed-income fund returning less than inflation) is an “economic loss”. Fixed income is only a short-term parking spot for money, like the emergency bucket.
Part of your assets in gold or silver to protect purchasing power.
Having cash doesn’t mean it’s time to buy; the time to buy is when the asset is good value.
And the most important investment: in yourself, through knowledge and awareness.

How big should the emergency fund be?
6 to 12 months of living costs
1 to 2 weeks of living costs
The size of one year’s dividends
Outside stocks, so a market drop doesn’t force you to sell.

When should you set aside your monthly savings?
At the start of the month, before spending
At the end of the month, whatever is left
Whenever the market turns up
Take your future self’s share first, then spend.
In FIS’s view, a fixed-income fund returning less than inflation is a good home for long-term capital.
Only for short-term parking; a return below inflation is an economic loss.
Your annual bonus has arrived. According to FIS, when do you buy stocks?
When a stock is good value, not just because you have money
The same day it arrives, with all of it, so you don’t fall behind inflation
Never; keep the bonus in a bank deposit only
The value of the asset decides when to buy, not your account balance.
Explain in your own words why money you need next year to buy a home shouldn’t go into stocks.

This money has a short horizon, and stocks can fall a lot within a year, say 40%; then you’d have to sell at a loss or delay buying the home. Money for 1 to 3 years belongs in fixed income, Akhza or gold, and only money you won’t need for 5 years or more goes into stocks.
This money’s horizon is short (under 3 years)
Stocks can drop sharply in the short run and you may be forced to sell at a loss
It belongs in fixed income, Akhza or gold; stocks are for money with a 5-year-plus horizon
The bucket rule: each sum of money goes where its horizon allows.
